problem: "an agent or a victim of the bowstring" becomes "the sultan's justice", losing the bowstring (strangling execution) image.
final_text: Seated on the carpet beside this basin was Mr. Rochester, wrapped in shawls, with a turban on his head. His dark eyes, swarthy skin, and exotic features suited the costume perfectly: he looked like an Eastern ruler, an agent or a victim of the executioner's bowstring. Presently Miss Ingram advanced into view. She too was dressed in oriental fashion: a crimson scarf tied like a sash around her waist, an embroidered handkerchief knotted about her temples, her beautifully shaped arms bare, one raised in the act of balancing a pitcher on her head. Her figure and features, her complexion and general air all suggested an Israelite princess from the days of the patriarchs—and that was clearly the character she intended to portray.

problem: "the more's the pity!" became the odd "the worse for it", and "that ruffian's rouge" (her ironic calling soot "rouge") was flattened to "grime".
final_text: "Alas, yes—more's the pity! Nothing could suit your complexion better than that ruffian's rouge."

problem: The source italicizes "_she could not charm him_", the emphatic climax of the paragraph; the edition keeps italics elsewhere (e.g. _your_, _then_) but drops them here.
final_text: I saw he was going to marry her for family, perhaps political reasons, because her rank and connections suited him. I felt he had not given her his love, and that her qualities were poorly suited to win it. This was the point—this was where the nerve was touched and teased—this was where the fever was kept alive: she could not charm him.

problem: "(figuratively) have died to them" loses "to them", and "one vital struggle with two tigers—jealousy and despair" loses the tigers image (paired with "heart torn out and devoured").
final_text: If she had won the victory outright, and he had yielded and sincerely laid his heart at her feet, I would have covered my face, turned to the wall, and (in a manner of speaking) died to them. If Miss Ingram had been a good and noble woman, gifted with strength, warmth, kindness, and sense, I would have fought one desperate battle with two tigers—jealousy and despair. Then, my heart torn out and devoured, I would have admired her, acknowledged her excellence, and been still for the rest of my days; and the more complete her superiority, the deeper my admiration, the more genuine my peace. But as things actually stood, to watch Miss Ingram's efforts at captivating Mr. Rochester, to see them fail again and again—while she remained blind to her failure, imagining each arrow struck home, preening herself on success while her pride and vanity drove further and further away the very thing she wanted to attract—to witness this was to be under constant excitement and ruthless restraint at the same time.

final_text: It was nearing dusk, and the clock had already warned that it was nearly time to dress for dinner, when little Adèle, who was kneeling beside me in the drawing room window seat, suddenly exclaimed—

final_text: He had spoken of Mr. Rochester as an old friend. Theirs must have been a curious friendship—a perfect example of the old saying that "extremes meet."

problem: Source: "she has taken a chair in the chimney-corner" (in the servants' hall, per 18.52). "By the kitchen fire" invents a location.
final_text: "But I can't persuade her to go, my lady," said the footman, "nor can any of the servants. Mrs. Fairfax is with her now, begging her to leave; but she has planted herself in a chair in the chimney corner and says nothing will shift her until she's allowed to come in here."

problem: "your organs of wonder and credulity are easily excited" loses "credulity" (and the phrenological "organs"), which is Blanche's actual jibe.
final_text: "Now, now, good people," returned Miss Ingram, "don't crowd me. Really, your organs of wonder and credulity are easily excited. You seem, judging by the importance you all—my good mama included—attach to this business, actually to believe we have a genuine witch in the house who is in league with the devil. I have seen a gypsy vagrant; she practised the standard tricks of palm reading and told me the usual things. My whim is satisfied; and now I think Mr. Eshton would do well to put the hag in the stocks tomorrow morning, as he threatened."

problem: Source: "attached undue importance to whatever revelations had been made her". The modern adds "than she wanted anyone to know", an invented motive.
final_text: Miss Ingram took up a book, leaned back in her chair, and refused further conversation. I watched her for nearly half an hour: during all that time she never turned a page, and her face grew steadily darker, more dissatisfied, and more sour with disappointment. She had clearly not heard anything to her advantage; and it seemed to me, from her prolonged gloom and silence, that despite her professed indifference she attached undue importance to whatever had been revealed to her.

problem: "I am sure she is something not right!" (uncanny, hedged) is hardened to "something supernatural".
final_text: "I am sure she is something not right!" they cried, one and all. "She told us such things! She knows everything about us!" And they sank breathlessly into the various seats the gentlemen hurried to bring them.

problem: "there is diablerie in the business after all" (devilry, witchcraft) becomes "something sinister", losing the supernatural sense Jane momentarily entertains.
final_text: "You do? Do you?" I thought. "So there is some devilry in this after all!"

problem: The sarcastic "A profound remark! A most ingenious quibble!" is reduced to "What a clever dodge!", dropping the mock-praise first exclamation.
final_text: "A profound remark! A most ingenious quibble! He went to Millcote this morning and will be back tonight or tomorrow. Does that remove him from your acquaintance—erase him from existence?"

problem: "blackaviced" (dark-complexioned) is rendered "dark-browed", which shifts the meaning to eyebrows/frowning.
final_text: "Appearances would suggest so. And no doubt (though, with an impudence that deserves correction, you seem to question it) they will make a supremely happy couple. He must love such a handsome, noble, witty, accomplished lady; and she probably loves him—or if not him, at least his purse. I know she considers the Rochester estate highly desirable; though (God forgive me!) I told her something about an hour ago on that subject that made her look very serious: the corners of her mouth dropped half an inch. I would advise her dark-complexioned suitor to watch out: if another comes along with a larger or clearer income, he is done for—"

problem: "The passions may rage furiously, like true heathens, as they are" drops the heathens simile, and "imagine all sorts of vain things" (Psalm 2 echo) becomes "impossible things".
final_text: "I see no obstacle to a happy outcome except in the brow; and that brow seems to say: 'I can live alone, if self-respect and circumstances require it. I need not sell my soul to buy happiness. I have an inner treasure born with me, which can sustain me if all outward joys are withheld—or offered only at a price I cannot afford.' The forehead declares: 'Reason sits firmly in control, and she will not let the feelings bolt and drag her into wild abysses. The passions may rage furiously, like the true heathens they are; desires may imagine all sorts of vain things; but judgment shall still have the last word in every argument and the deciding vote in every question. Strong wind, earthquake, and fire may pass; but I shall follow the guidance of that still small voice which speaks the dictates of conscience.'

final_text: "There, then—'Off, ye lendings!'" And Mr. Rochester stepped out of his disguise.

final_text: "No—some impossible one. In short, I believe you have been trying to draw me out—or draw me in. You have been talking nonsense to make me talk nonsense. It is hardly fair, sir."

final_text: "Fetch me a glass of wine, Jane, from the dining room. They will be at supper there. And tell me if Mason is with them, and what he is doing."
